title: The Gathering

choices.label: Look at them.
choices.resultText: You look at them, every one, the living and the held, and the Register writes down who came, each in their own hand. It takes a while. Nobody hurries you. Tonight, for the first time in a year, there is nowhere else to be.

title: The Council
Answer Him
body:
There are three ways to answer him. Tonight only one of them can be yours.

The Register lays them out on a clean page, in your hand, the way it took down your stated intention on the morning of the Trial: three lines, and a margin.

Whatever you answer, the hall will hold you to it. Once the door is open there is no taking it back.

choices.label: Restoration: put the Seal back.
choices.resultText: You say it, and the Register writes it in your hand and underlines it once: Restoration. He was wrong, you will tell him, or the price was too high; either way you are putting it back. It will need every piece you brought home. It will need someone to stay in it.

choices.label: Dominion: take what he opened.
choices.resultText: You say it, and the Register writes it in your hand and underlines it once: Dominion. He was right, you will tell him, and what he opened is yours now. Somewhere in the hall someone lets out a breath, and somewhere else someone holds one.

choices.label: Synthesis: make the Seal breathe.
choices.resultText: You say it, and the Register writes it in your hand and underlines it once: Synthesis. Half of what he read was true, you will tell him, and so was half of what he broke. You mean to make the Seal something the world can breathe through. The Register reads the line back to itself twice, as if to be sure it says what it says.

title: Not Everyone
body:
Not everyone in the hall agrees with you.

The Register writes down who: {dissenter_names}. Each name goes down in the hand it belongs to.

Everyone on that line came through the edge on your word, and tonight will stand where you put them. When it is over, everyone on that line will go. Nobody says so. Nobody has to.

choices.label: Thank them anyway.
choices.resultText: You thank them. You get a nod for it, and no more. It is not agreement. It is something you will remember longer.

title: The Nod
body:
Before you open the door you go down to the foot of the dais, where the Examiner has stood since the morning of your Trial, caught in the middle of a nod. You take your place on the examination floor, at the distance she likes.

{nod_progress}

You report, one last time: that you have answered him, and that you are going to open the door.

The nod finishes.

It is a small thing. Her chin comes down the last hair of its travel, and stops there, and stays. Of everything in the hall, it is the first thing to finish. She still has not said what she thinks. She is keeping it, you understand, until the board has had its say.

'Be it recorded,' says the Register, very quietly, 'that the Examiner has nodded.' It underlines it twice.

title: The East Doors
body:
You walk down the hall between the families and the frozen Keepers, to the east doors, and stand in them. You are the door. You have been told so often enough.

You open.

The edge goes out of you like a held breath let go, all the way around the Anchorhold at once, and through the east doors, where the courtyard has always been, there is a hall.

It is this hall, as the running world kept it. It has no roof. Grass grows between the stones of the examination floor, and rain is coming down on the empty dais and the empty cradle, and at the far end, where the stair goes up behind the dais, a lamp is lit in a high window. Where the two floors meet the rain comes in through the doors, and stops in the air above the dry stones of the afternoon, and hangs there, the way everything in here hangs.

Then, in here, everything that is his begins to move.

The Keepers in the doorway finish their step, and take another.

{spell_fate}

{warden_watch}

You go back up the hall to the lectern, to your place, and stand in front of the letter of ink in the air. Behind you the Keepers come on, unhurried. Beyond the rain someone is reading toward the door, line by line, the way he reads everything. The door is open. He can see it now.

'Be it recorded,' says the Register, 'that the door is open.' And then, because it cannot help itself: 'Once.'

title: The Other Hand
A Second Time
With Him
The Hall Holds
The Rebinding
The Breach
body:
The wound in the sphere is right there.

Inside the Second it is still the instant it happened: six shards a finger's width apart, and between them, where the Seal was, a breach no wider than a hand, fresh, still opening. Through it, very faintly, comes the sound of something enormous turning over in its sleep.

You do not close it. You put your hand into it.

It is like putting your hand into a river at night: cold, then not cold, then nothing at all but the pull. Everything he opened is on the other side of it, moving, belonging to nobody.

The pieces you brought home turn in the glass to face the breach, the way a hall turns to face a door. They are not keys tonight.

The breach widens to let you through.

title: Between
body:
The wound in the sphere is right there.

Inside the Second it is still the instant it happened: six shards a finger's width apart, and between them, where the Seal was, a breach no wider than a hand, fresh, still opening. Through it, very faintly, comes the sound of something enormous turning over in its sleep.

You do not close it, and you do not go through it. You stand in it: in the place between the glass and whatever is on the other side, where nobody has ever stood, and you listen.

Something on the other side is listening back.

It is not a voice. Under your arm the Register opens by itself to a clean page, and something begins to write on it in a hand the Register has never held: letters like weather, like frost growing on a window, like nothing at all.

'Be it recorded,' the Register whispers, 'that it can read.'

title: The First Question
body:
When the fighting stops, the hand that is not a hand writes again on the clean page, slowly, as if it were learning letters by watching yours.

The Register reads it out, because somebody has to. 'It asks,' says the Register, 'what the wall was for.'

choices.label: 'Both. It kept you out, and it kept magic in.'
choices.resultText: The hand on the page goes still for a long time. Then it writes one mark under your answer. The Register cannot read it, and copies it anyway. It looks like agreement. It looks like a door left on the latch.

choices.label: 'Both. A man wrote me sixty pages to say so, and it did not help him.'
choices.resultText: The hand on the page goes still. Then it writes one mark under your answer, the way a reader marks a line worth coming back to.

choices.label: 'A rule with two clauses. Everyone only ever read one of them.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes the rule out under yours, both clauses, in letters like frost. It has been reading the other clause for a very long time.

choices.label: 'To keep you out.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes nothing. After a while the Register turns the page for it, as if to spare everyone.

choices.label: 'To starve the world. He was right about that.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes nothing. The Register, very primly, writes your answer down in your hand and does not underline it.

title: The Second Question
body:
The hand writes again, faster now, as if it had found its way into the language.

'It asks,' says the Register, 'what it cost. The opening. It wants to know what it cost.'

choices.label: 'People. They count themselves, every one.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes your answer under its question, and then a long row of small marks after it, one for each, as if it had been told to count.

choices.label: 'People. A woman who opened a gate for her dead told me their names.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes your answer under its question, and then a long row of small marks after it, one for each. It does not stop until the line runs off the page.

choices.label: 'Names. Someone in my guild reads them aloud once a year.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes nothing for a moment. Then, slowly, it begins to copy names off the facing page of the Register, where the honored dead are kept, as if it wanted to learn them.

choices.label: 'A stone by a road, with my name first on it.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes your name. It is the first thing it has written that the Register can read, and the Register goes very quiet.

choices.label: 'The dead. Ask them. They keep better accounts than he does.'
choices.resultText: Something on the other side of the breach asks them. You feel it go past you, the way you feel a draft. When it comes back, the hand writes your answer again, underlined.

choices.label: 'A price. He paid it once.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes your answer back to you, word for word, and leaves it there, the way a teacher leaves a wrong sum on the board.

choices.label: 'Whatever it cost, it's paid.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes nothing. On the other side of the breach something waits to see whether you will try again.

title: The Third Question
body:
The last line the hand writes is short. It underlines it, which you did not know it could do.

'It asks,' says the Register, and for once its voice is not steady, 'what you are.'

choices.label: 'The blank in his margin.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes a word under your answer, and then, carefully, crosses it out, the way he has crossed out every line around you for a year. Then it writes it again, and leaves it.

choices.label: 'A sentence somebody started, and left blank on purpose.'
choices.resultText: The hand draws a line from your answer to the edge of the page and off it, into the margin, as if pointing at someone who is not there.

choices.label: 'The one he apologized to.'
choices.resultText: The hand stops. It seems to understand apology. It writes something small under your answer that the Register will not read aloud.

choices.label: 'A second somebody spent, so I could stand in it.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes the second out, all of it, in one stroke that does not end, and the Register lets it run off the page.

choices.label: 'A wizard.'
choices.resultText: The hand waits, as if for the rest of the sentence. There is no rest of the sentence. That, it seems, is the trouble.

choices.label: 'None of your business.'
choices.resultText: The hand writes nothing. On the other side of the breach something that has been refused a great deal, but never to its face, considers the experience.

title: The Reckoning
The Next Line
body:
Halfway through, he stops.

Not because he is beaten. He stands in the middle of the examination floor with his hands open, and looks at the hall the way a man looks at a page that has gone blank under his eyes.

'I cannot read anything,' he says. 'Not you. Not the room. Not the next line.' He turns his hands over and looks at them. 'I have not been without the next line since I was nine years old.'

On the clean page under your arm the hand that is not a hand writes something, and the Register reads it out, very carefully: 'It says it has been reading him for a long time.'

He laughs once, without much in it. 'Of course it has,' he says. 'Everything reads. I only thought I would be the one who finished.'

Then he lifts his hands again.

title: Not As Read
body:
{his_last}

He goes up the steps of the dais slowly, the way a man goes up to bed, and sits down in his chair.

The Second takes him the way it took the afternoon. Between one breath and the next he is still: a man with ink on one finger, looking at the lectern. The Astrologer's chair is not empty anymore.

'Be it recorded,' says the Register, and stops, and for a long moment does not go on. Then, in its own hand, very small: 'Not as read.'

title: Restoration
Dominion
body:
When it is over the breach does not close. It stays open the width of a hand, and it is yours.

You can feel it the way you feel your own hand: everything he opened, all of it on the other side, moving, and none of it belonging to anyone but you. When you want it to come, it comes. When you want it to stop, it stops. Mostly.

Out in the running world the leaks become wells. In farm villages children light candles nobody taught them to light, and the schools fill, and the Fast rings its bells for the dead and does not stop ringing them. Things still come up through the seep. Nobody has read where it stops. Now it is your hand that has to.

The Register writes it all down in your hand, as it always has, and once, halfway down the page, it stops and looks for a long moment at a letter it has just written, as if it did not recognize it.

{warden_held}

title: Synthesis
body:
You do not close the breach, and you do not keep it. You change it.

It takes the rest of the night. Piece by piece, with the other hand writing beside yours on the clean page, you set the Seal back into the glass, not as a wall but as a weave: six refusals with room between them, a membrane the world can breathe through that will still hold back the flood. When it is done the glass is whole, and not quite clear, like a window with weather on it.

Out in the running world magic comes back slowly, as much as the world can hold and no more. Some spells stop working the way they used to and start working some other way. The seep still comes in, by measures, and something on the far side of it is paying attention. Nobody can read where any of it goes. Not him. Not you.

The sky over the Anchorhold has not moved since the naming. Tonight, for the first time, you have the feeling that it is reading you back.

{warden_held}
